name: Refuses, and the app shows the cut-off refusal as the verdict
cause: The prompt insists on a side-on photo; on anything else the model hedges ("I'm unable to classify…"). max_tokens=5 truncates the hedge, the string match finds neither label, and the fragment is shown to the user. 8 of the 12 front/back photos end here.

name: Front and back views: guesses or refuses instead of saying it can't judge
cause: Only 4 of 12 front/back photos come out right. The arch is invisible from the front; the model has no field for "can't see the spine", so it either refuses (row above) or answers with side-view confidence.

name: Misses a clear arch (calls a banana back "good form")
cause: Legs split or bent, silhouettes at dusk, and a low-resolution copy. The model reads the leg line as the body line; when the torso has no contrast it defaults to "good form". 049 is the downscaled copy of a photo it labels correctly at full size.

name: Over-calls an arch on straight-ish photos (my score 3 to 5)
cause: Slightly piked hips, a one-arm balance, a night shot and a dark garage. Dark or unusual photos push it toward "banana back", the label its examples describe in most detail.

name: Coin-flip on borderline photos: different answers across the five runs
cause: Temperature 0 does not make the arg-max stable when the two labels are nearly tied. These are the photos a 0–10 score would place at 4 to 6; the binary prompt has no way to express that.

name: Controls: no way to say "not a handstand"
cause: Six of seven controls are refused, which is the right instinct shown as a broken message. The bronze statue of a handstand is scored "banana back" five times out of five.
